newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Hong Kong aviation has bright future- Boeing chief.
newsitem.headline: Hong Kong aviation has bright future- Boeing chief.

text.p: Single aisle jets will account for 73 per cent of all aircraft deliveries to Hong Kong and China over the next 20 years, Mike Zimmerman president of Boeing China said.

In a speech at the Hong Kong International Aerospace Forum, Zimmerman also said the Hong Kong and China market will account for $110 billion worth of orders or one tenth of the world total for new aircraft over the next 20 years. More than 1,900 jets are required in the Greater China region which will experience the fastest air travel growth rate anywhere in the world.
The "future could not be brighter" for Hong Kong's aviation industry," Zimmerman stated.

"We believe the air market will be seven times larger by 2016 than it is today. Naturally this is good news for Hong Kong whose importance will continue to rise following the handover. The reasons are obvious: Hong Kong is central to China's trade, banking and other dealings with the world. So as China's economy grows, so will Hong Kong's. As we stand on the threshold of a new era, aviation will continue to be the driving force behind this region's success," he said.
The opening of Hong Kong's new "aerial gateway" at Chek Lap Kok would further consolidate the territory's position as the region's premier aviation hub, he added.

IATA statistics show air travel in Asia will rise from 135 million trips per year now to 400 million trips per year by the year 2010 with business travel accounting for much of this "explosive" growth aided by Chinese nationals becoming tourists.
The growth in the single aisle market of aircraft such as the Boeing 737, 757 and Airbus A320 is due to rapid development of point to point services within China.
New aircraft would also be available to fly from Hong Kong to New York non-stop within five years, the Boeing executive said.
Zimmerman criticised the U.S. government's China policy and called for normal trade relations with Beijing to aid Boeing sales.
"They should not be put through MFN (Most Favoured Nation) every year," Zimmerman said. - Reuters Air Cargo Service Tel+ 44 171 542 7706 Fax +5017 - www.racs.com
